doc: The OpenInference dialect. Its messages arrive as *indexed attribute families* - a list of objects flattened into dotted keys, because OTel attributes are a flat map - and its retrieval spans report documents the same way. The one thing that is not a plain read is the multimodal overlay: the dotted keys lose file blocks and redact URLs, while a serialised `input.value` on the same span holds the whole content, so the richer copy is joined on by position.

carriers.doc: On an OpenInference TOOL span, `output.value` is the result of this one execution rather than accumulated framework state. The observation-type qualifier makes this strictly narrower than the generic `output.value` carrier.

On an OpenInference LLM span, `output.value` is the serialised response of this one call, listing its parts in the order the model returned them. Still accumulated state - it may repeat what the flattened `llm.output_messages` already states - but its positions order the parts even where that flattened copy is the one kept, because the flattening separates content from tool calls and loses which came first. The observation-type qualifier makes this strictly narrower than the generic `output.value` carrier.
What this span produced, as an indexed array.

The conversation this span received, as an indexed array. Its members are separate attribute keys that are one array, so they carry an ordering family: `llm.input_messages.0.message` and `.1.message` are one sequence, and the order resolver needs to know that to sequence a request's own new turns. That fact used to be a hardcoded key comparison in the resolver, which is precisely the shape of framework knowledge this engine exists to hold instead.
The result set produced by one retrieval span.
The candidate documents handed to one reranker span.
The ordered result set produced by one reranker span.
The query handed to one reranker span.

detect.doc: The generic OpenInference dialect, after every framework that rides on it.
detect.label: OpenInference

rendering.doc: Smolagents writes its `Calling tools` and `Observation` bookkeeping back into the next model request under these pseudo-roles. The model was sent them, so the span shows them; the structured model output and the TOOL span are the lossless call and result, so the trace and session views keep those instead.

overlay.doc: The flattened family loses whole content blocks and writes `__REDACTED__` for a url, while this dialect's serialised copy of the same conversation keeps both - so where both describe one message, the richer one is preferred. Matched by position, and only for an entry whose content arrived flattened.

any.doc: This dialect writes a message class path as an array. Asked of every member, not the first: a list may open with a shape that omits it.

A Chat Completions request body, which the OpenAI instrumentor serialises whole and flattens message by message. Its system turn sits inside the list, so the list is indexed exactly as the family is. A request whose system prompt sits beside the list (Converse, Messages) would shift every position by one, which is why a role list alone is not enough.

overlay.doc: The same loss on the way out: the flattened family drops blocks it has no name for, such as reasoning, and indexes what remains from where it sat - so an answer that followed its reasoning arrives as `contents.1` with nothing at `contents.0`. The dialect's serialised generation on the same span keeps every block in order. Matched by position, one generation per output message, and only for an entry whose content arrived flattened.

witness.doc: A generation's message carries its class path as an array.

messages.doc: The return value of a generic OpenInference TOOL span that identifies itself with the convention's tool.id attribute. The dedicated generic scope distinguishes direct OITracer use from framework instrumentors that own another result carrier.

AutoGen's TOOL span records the result as the Python `str()` of what the tool returned (and labels it `text/plain`, which is that rendering's MIME type, not the value's), so a dict arrives single-quoted. Read as the value it renders; a result that is not a whole Python container falls through to `openinference.tool_output` and is read as JSON or text.

The return value of an OpenInference TOOL span from AutoGen. AutoGen 0.7.5 records the call id on its sibling semantic-convention span rather than this OpenInference span, so the result keeps the tool name and query-time correlation links it to the oldest unclaimed call of that name.
What a retrieval returned. One message holding every document, not one each: they are a result set, and splitting them would read as a conversation.
The documents a reranker was given.
The order it put them in.
The query a reranker scored against.
The text an embedding span turned into a vector.

The same family's names, projected from each schema's function definition. A separate rule because a name list and a definition list are different observations - one says which tools were available, the other what they take.

This dialect's tool definitions, in the order it reports them: the indexed family first, then the flat list, and the single-tool triple only if neither produced anything. The primary order is the *emission* order where both forms coexist, and persistence keeps it - so it is the retired rank order, not an arbitrary one. A branch set rather than three rules with presence gates, because 'nothing was produced' is the condition the retired code tested.

primary.doc: Tool schemas as an indexed family, one JSON schema per entry. The entry is a wrapper around that schema, so the projection names the leaf that is the datum - an entry without one is not this shape and contributes nothing. Aggregated because a tool list is one observation, not one per tool. A payload that does not parse is dropped: a malformed schema is not a tool definition, and an indexed member is otherwise sniffed to the string it is.
This dialect's tool schemas, in one attribute, elements possibly serialised.

fallback_if_primary_empty.doc: One tool per span, written as three separate attributes. Read only if this dialect's list carriers produced nothing - the branch order tests *production*, where an `attr_exists` gate tested only presence and a malformed list suppressed a perfectly good triple. Still gated on the convention's own single-tool attribute, which outranks a dialect's spelling of the same fact whether or not this dialect produced anything.

span_facts.doc: This dialect states a span's kind directly, in capitals.
